STEP 1 - Scene: A small snack/side plate of raw or lightly prepared produce: one large apple, cherry tomatoes, carrot sticks, and corn rounds (cut cobs).

STEP 2 - Vessel: Oval serving platter, roughly 30 x 20 cm. Treat as a large dish with an effective diameter of about 26 cm. Area ≈ 3.14 x 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Apple (large, whole)
- Cherry tomatoes (about 4 visible)
- Carrot pieces (about 6-7 sticks/rounds)
- Corn pieces (2 cut rounds)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of vessel):
- Apple: ~80 cm² → 15%
- Cherry tomatoes: ~35 cm² → 7%
- Carrots: ~60 cm² → 11%
- Corn: ~60 cm² → 11%
Total food coverage ≈ 44%.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x height):
- Apple: 80 cm² x 7 cm ≈ 560 ml (whole fruit envelope; apple is roughly a sphere ~9.5 cm across, so about 300 ml actual; use ~300 ml)
- Cherry tomatoes: 35 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 88 ml
- Carrots: 60 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 150 ml
- Corn: 60 cm² x 4 cm ≈ 240 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Apple: 300 ml x 0.6 ≈ 180 g
- Cherry tomatoes: 88 ml x 0.6 ≈ 53 g
- Carrots: 150 ml x 0.6 ≈ 90 g
- Corn: 240 ml x 0.6 ≈ 144 g
Total ≈ 467 g.

STEP 7 - Energy (kcal/100 g, raw):
- Apple: 52 kcal → 180 g → 94 kcal
- Cherry tomatoes: 18 kcal → 53 g → 10 kcal
- Carrots: 41 kcal → 90 g → 37 kcal
- Corn (sweet corn, raw kernels/cob): 86 kcal → 144 g → 124 kcal
Total ≈ 265 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 470 g of mostly raw produce covering under half a platter is plausible. Mostly low-calorie produce with corn and apple driving energy, so ~265 kcal is reasonable.

Estimated total: about 470 g and about 265 kcal.
